title: Chain rule (Leibniz notation)
ced_evidence: FUN-3.C.1 "The chain rule provides a way to differentiate composite functions"; Developing Understanding: "dy/dx = dy/du · du/dx"

hooks.hook_text: Times the derivative of what's inside

expands_to.means: multiply by the derivative of the inner function u(x)

hooks.when_to_use: Say it each time you differentiate an outer function, so you do not forget the inner derivative.
hooks.caution: In written work, show the explicit inner-derivative factor (e.g. du/dx or g'(x)). Also differentiate the outer function with the inner function left unchanged inside it.

title: Chain rule for a composite f(g(x))
ced_evidence: FUN-3.C "Calculate derivatives of compositions of differentiable functions"

title: Composite function: outer and inner functions
body: A composite function is a function embedded in another function; to differentiate it, decompose it into an outer function and an inner function, where y is a function of u and u is a function of x.
caution: Common errors are misidentifying the inner function and forgetting to differentiate it. The chain rule also applies to sin²x, tan(2x − 1), and e^{x²}.
ced_evidence: Building the Mathematical Practices: "decompose composite functions into their 'outer' and 'inner' component functions"

title: Chain rule applied to y in implicit differentiation
caution: y depends on x, so every term containing y needs the factor dy/dx. This includes y in expressions such as y/(3y² − x).
ced_evidence: FUN-3.D.1 "The chain rule is the basis for implicit differentiation"; Preparing for the AP Exam: "the chain rule applies to y because y depends on x"

title: Second and higher-order derivatives
body: Differentiating f′ produces the second derivative f″, provided the derivative of f′ exists, and repeating this process produces higher-order derivatives of f.
ced_evidence: FUN-3.F.1 "Differentiating f′ produces the second derivative f″, provided the derivative of f′ exists"

title: Notations for higher-order derivatives
body: For y = f(x), the second derivative is written in these ways, and the nth derivative has its own notations.

items.label: d²y/dx²
items.meaning: Leibniz notation for the second derivative

items.label: f″(x)
items.meaning: prime notation for the second derivative

items.label: y″
items.meaning: prime notation for the second derivative of y

items.label: dⁿy/dxⁿ
items.meaning: Leibniz notation for the nth derivative

ced_evidence: FUN-3.F.2 "notations for the second derivative include d²y/dx², f″(x), and y″ ... dⁿy/dxⁿ or f⁽ⁿ⁾(x)"
